title: Review: jmap-mail-types (round 2)
description: Second review pass of jmap-mail-types after fixes from JMAP-ez5. Scope: all source files in crate-jmap-mail-types/src/.
notes:
Maintainer risk: LOW — No correctness bugs that fire immediately. One P1 doc mismatch (Email partial deserialization) will generate confused user issues when partial Email/get is attempted. One P2 construction-time validation gap on header field. Wire types are spec-faithful. All types are non-exhaustive. No unsafe, no async leakage.
Confidence: 8% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: the Email partial deserialization issue — need to verify whether RFC 8620 §5.1 guarantees id is always returned and whether any metadata field can ever be legitimately absent in a non-partial response. Uncertainty driven by: not running against a real JMAP server fixture. Would raise confidence if: added a test that tries partial deserialization and verifies the failure.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — No unsafe, no unwrap in production code, no gratuitous clones, no Box<dyn Error> in API. Main concerns: Mailbox::new has too many arguments (lint suppressed without explanation), Email::new requires pre-built HashMap making the common case verbose. The string_enum macro is clean. Keyword trait impls are thorough and correct.
Rust idiom confidence: 12% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: Email::new HashMap ergonomics (may be intentional given JMAP wire format semantics). Uncertainty driven by: did not examine test files for test-quality issues.
